Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small, hypoplastic right lung with diffuse opacity and marked dextroposition of the heart (shifted to the right), which are hallmark features of Scimitar syndrome. While the classic "scimitar" vein is best visualized on the CT scans (Figures 4 and 5), Option B correctly describes the characteristic plain film findings of right lung hypoplasia and ipsilateral mediastinal shift associated with this condition.
